origin.task: User-directed Frank v0.1 sandbox integration, organ/module conservation, runtime hardening and live-research feedback

sandbox_results.f7_runtime_spine: PASS: stale state fails closed before central open; doctor read-only; boot-once state join only/no model

new_negative_result.finding: The newly added F6 endpoint-boundary regression dynamically loaded a dataclass-bearing adapter without first registering the module in sys.modules. Python 3.13 failed during @dataclass processing before the security regression executed.
new_negative_result.repair: Register dynamic module in sys.modules before exec_module and remove it on failed import.

architecture_delta.organ_conservation: No historical function is deletable merely because its old process/service boundary disappears. RETAIN/FUSE/EMERGENT_DISTRIBUTE/REPLACED_WITH_LINEAGE remain implementation transformations, not permission to erase function or evidence.
architecture_delta.technical_module_plane: 34 named legacy service/module surfaces now have an executable sandbox conservation overlay on Frank main.
architecture_delta.runtime_migration: Schema chains are now atomic per physical SQLite DB on Frank main; ClayGraph migrates before authoritative UnifiedDB; pair-wide crash atomicity is not claimed and divergent materialization must fail closed.
architecture_delta.local_model_boundary: F6 local endpoint admission now remains fail-closed across redirects and malformed endpoint forms.
architecture_delta.f7: Minimal doctor + boot-once runtime spine exists and is sandbox-regression compatible. It is not a complete daemon/package.

open_gap.rule: Do not fabricate unnamed legacy module identities to reach 74/74. Recover them from primary archive/process/code evidence and attach function/state/measurement/rollback lineage before declaring complete coverage.

live_research_feedback.sqlite: Use integrity_check together with foreign_key_check; WAL is part of persistent state while active and must be handled by backup/recovery correctly.
live_research_feedback.model_serving: Keep Frank engine-neutral behind an OpenAI-compatible local boundary; llama.cpp and vLLM currently provide compatible local serving surfaces, but engine choice remains measurement-driven.

feedback.frank: Continue composing the current main runtime into one executable sandbox product. Preserve the 74-measured/34-named gap as a blocker for full legacy inventory claims, not as a blocker to fusing already-recovered functions.
feedback.harness: Use both cognitive-organ lineage and technical-module lineage. Any fused/emergent successor must remain lesionable/readable/reconstructable in tests.
feedback.unifieddb: Retain per-DB atomic migration and add foreign_key_check plus interruption/recovery cases to acceptance evidence.
feedback.claygraph: Keep derived-state rebuildability and authority separation while testing whether physical collapse remains possible without losing diagnostic graph semantics.
feedback.gwt: Count receiver use/re-entry, not broadcast presence alone. Preserve current-prompt priority and lesion/rescue handles inside a collapsed implementation.
feedback.hyperposition: Preserve unresolved alternatives and prevent proposal state from becoming effect authority during module collapse.
feedback.emergenz: Do not call implementation collapse emergence. Require causal lesion/rescue/re-entry and null comparisons.
feedback.claycode: Represent successor lineage and rollback handles as typed transition contracts so old module names can disappear physically without losing testability.
feedback.clayresearch: Propagate the Python 3.13 dynamic-import test failure as implementation-negative evidence and keep sandbox receipts separate from target-host release evidence.
feedback.clay: Use the 7/7 composite sandbox result as a current integration gate, then continue collapsing boundaries only behind matched before/after tests.
